title: Isolation of Nuclei from Frozen Tissue for Epigenomic and Transcriptomic Assays
author: Adam Turner
materials: Prepare all buffers. For faster dissolution, crush protease inhibitor tablets prior to addition to 1x Homogenization Buffer Unstable Solution. DTT, Spermidine, and Spermine are stored at -20 °C . All other detergents, Multiome wash buffer, and other buffers are stored at 4 °C . Keep all buffers on ice. Do not prepare transposition mix ahead of time. Remember that the catalog number provided for Iodixanol from Sigma comes as a 60% solution (not 100%).
Dounce with “B” tight pestle for 20 strokes.

steps.title: Pre‑chill equipment and tubes
steps.instruction: Set all swinging‑bucket and fixed‑angle centrifuges to 4 °C. Pre‑chill both Dounce homogenizers, pestles, and all LoBind tubes (2 mL round‑bottom, 1.5 mL LoBind, 2 mL Nunc cryotube, 50 mL conical) in a 4 °C refrigerator.

steps.title: Prepare water bath for cleaning
steps.instruction: Fill a 2 L beaker with 500 mL sterile water; this will be used to soak Dounces and pestles after use.

steps.title: Retrieve frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Remove tissue samples from liquid nitrogen storage, keep on dry ice until processing.

steps.title: Thaw tissue in Dounce with HBUS
steps.instruction: Place 20 mg frozen tissue into a pre‑chilled 2 mL Dounce containing 1 mL cold 1× HBUS; let thaw on ice for 10 min. For >30 mg tissue use 2 mL 1× HBUS, for 10–20 mg use 1 mL, and for 50 µm sections use 0.5 mL.

steps.title: Dounce with loose pestle A
steps.instruction: Using pestle “A” (loose), dounce the suspension until resistance disappears (≈10 strokes).

steps.title: Optional pre‑crush fibrous tissue
steps.instruction: If tissue is fibrous (e.g., heart, muscle), pre‑chill a mortar and pestle on dry ice and manually crush tissue into small chunks (do not pulverize to powder).

steps.title: Optional filter homogenate
steps.instruction: If residual un‑homogenized tissue hinders Douncing, filter the homogenate through a 70 µm bucket‑style cell strainer into a pre‑chilled 50 mL conical before using tight pestle “B”.

steps.title: Transfer homogenate through Flowmi strainer
steps.instruction: Load the homogenate into a 1 mL pipette tip fitted with a 70 µm Flowmi filter, then transfer the filtered material into a pre‑chilled 2 mL LoBind tube. Repeat until the entire volume has been filtered and transferred.

steps.title: Clean Dounce and pestles
steps.instruction: Rinse all Dounces and pestles thoroughly with sterile water (2 ×), then with 70 % ethanol (2 ×). Place pestle “A” and pestle “B” in the beaker of sterile water for later cleaning. Let dry on a Kimwipe or paper towel for a few hours to overnight.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei by low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the LoBind tube at 350 rcf, 4 °C for 5 min in a fixed‑angle rotor.

steps.title: Remove supernatant, leave 50 µL
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate all supernatant leaving exactly 50 µL (contains cytoplasmic components).

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei to 400 µL 1× HB
steps.instruction: Add cold 1× HB to reach a total volume of 400 µL (e.g., add 350 µL if 50 µL remained). Pipette gently until nuclei are fully resuspended without clumps.

steps.title: Add 50 % Iodixanol (RNasin) and mix
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (400 µL) of 50 % Iodixanol solution containing RNasin Plus RNase inhibitor; mix well by pipetting.

steps.title: Layer 30 % Iodixanol under mixture
steps.instruction: Slowly layer 600 µL of 30 % Iodixanol (with RNasin Plus) beneath the 25 %/50 % mixture.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the outside of the pipette tip with a Kimwipe to remove excess Iodixanol.
Push the pipette only to the first stop to avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Layer 40 % Iodixanol under 30 % layer
steps.instruction: Slowly layer 600 µL of 40 % Iodixanol (with RNasin Plus) beneath the 30 % layer.

substeps.instruction: Wipe the outside of the pipette tip with a Kimwipe.
Push the pipette only to the first stop to prevent mixing and bubbles.

steps.title: Gradient centrifugation at 3000 rcf
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a pre‑chilled swinging‑bucket centrifuge and spin for 20 min at 3000 rcf, 4 °C, brake off. Handle tubes gently to avoid disturbing the gradient.

steps.title: Aspirate top layers to 200–300 µL above band
steps.instruction: Using a vacuum aspirator, remove the top layers until 200–300 µL of liquid remains above the nuclei band located at the 30 %–40 % interface. Do not aspirate more than 200 µL at once to avoid disturbing the band.

steps.title: Collect nuclei band
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µL pipette tip, place the tip just above the 30 %–40 % interface, circle the tip back‑and‑forth while slowly releasing the plunger to “vacuum” up the nuclei band (~200 µL) and transfer to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Count nuclei (Trypan Blue or ethidium)
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of nuclei to a clean 1.5 mL tube, add 10 µL Trypan Blue, mix and load 10 µL onto a disposable hemocytometer slide (or use an automatic cell counter). For samples with debris, mix 10 µL nuclei with 10 µL 1 µM ethidium homodimer‑I (1 mM stock diluted 1:100) and count RFP‑positive nuclei on a fluorescence‑compatible counter.

substeps.instruction: If using a hemocytometer, count nuclei in the four large corner squares and multiply total by 5 000 to obtain nuclei/µL.
If using a fluorescence counter, record the RFP‑positive count.

steps.title: Optional cryopreserve extra nuclei
steps.instruction: Pellet remaining nuclei by centrifugation for 10 min at 500 rcf, 4 °C. Aspirate supernatant using two pipetting steps (p1000 then p200). Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL cold BAM Banker media, transfer to a pre‑chilled 2 mL Nunc cryovial, and slow‑freeze in a controlled‑rate freezing container before storing at –80 °C or in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Thaw nuclei on ice or use directly
steps.instruction: If nuclei were cryopreserved, thaw on ice before proceeding; otherwise use freshly isolated nuclei immediately.

steps.title: Aliquot nuclei into Multiome Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Aliquot the desired number of nuclei into 1 mL of Multiome Wash Buffer in a 1.5 mL Lo‑Bind tube. Gently invert the tube 5 times.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei at 500 rcf
steps.instruction: Spin at 500 rcf, 4 °C for 5 min in a fixed‑angle rotor; a small pellet should be visible if >25 000 nuclei were present.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant (p1000 then p200)
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant using two pipetting steps: first with a p1000 pipette, then with a p200 pipette, as described previously.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in Diluted Nuclei Buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in the desired volume of 1× Diluted Nuclei Buffer (recipe as in Materials). Add 1–2 % BSA to reduce clumping.

steps.title: Prepare transposition mix on ice
steps.instruction: On ice, combine ATAC Buffer B (PN‑2000193) and ATAC Enzyme B (PN‑2000265/PN‑2000272) to make the transposition mix; pipette 10×, vortex briefly, and spin down.

steps.title: Add nuclei to transposition mix
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of nuclei stock to 10 µL of transposition mix (total 15 µL). Mix by pipetting up and down 6 times (set pipette to 10 µL). Do not centrifuge or vortex; avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Incubate transposition reaction
steps.instruction: Place the reaction in a thermal cycler for 1 h at 37 °C; set lid temperature to 50 °C. Reaction volume should be 15 µL.

steps.title: Proceed with 10x Multiome downstream steps
steps.instruction: Continue with the steps described in the 10x Genomics Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression User Guide (CG000338).

steps.title: Add RNasin for RNA‑based assay
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL RNasin Plus RNase Inhibitor per mL of 1× HBUS as instructed in the Same‑Day Buffers section and mix well.

steps.title: High‑volume wash for pooling samples
steps.instruction: For pooling, transfer each sample’s nuclei to a pre‑chilled 15 mL Falcon tube, then add ice‑cold Multiome Wash Buffer up to 15 mL total. Invert the tube up and down 5 times.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 250 rcf, 4 °C for 10 min in a pre‑chilled large swinging‑bucket centrifuge; a pellet should be visible.
Aspirate supernatant down to ~1 mL with a 10 mL serological pipette, then remove to 200 µL with a p1000 pipette, and finally remove the last 200 µL with a p200 pipette without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the pooled nuclei pellet in 100 µL of Diluted Nuclei Buffer (adjust volume if a different final concentration is required). Pipette up and down 10 times gently on ice.

steps.title: Adjust final nuclei concentration
steps.instruction: Take 10 µL of the pooled nuclei, add 10 µL Trypan Blue (or ethidium homodimer‑I) and count as before. Adjust the concentration to ~5 000 nuclei/µL (or the desired value) by adding more Diluted Nuclei Buffer. Typical loading uses 5 µL of nuclei (≈25 000 nuclei) per transposition reaction.

steps.title: Final nuclei ready for assays
steps.instruction: The nuclei are now ready for ATAC transposition, single‑nucleus RNA‑seq, or cryopreservation as described. They may also be used directly in downstream epigenomic and transcriptomic assays.
